verdict.rationale: Qodo supports persistent, centralized conventions via rule systems, configuration-as-code, org/repo-level settings, and 'Rule Miner' which generates rules from past PR history — a concrete mechanism for building memory of past review decisions and applying them going forward (qodo-docs-11, qodo-docs-12, qodo-docs-13, qodo-docs-10). Code governance features also track a history of findings/decisions across the codebase (qodo-docs-14, qodo-docs-15). However, evidence doesn't show adaptive learning from reviewer feedback/dismissals over time, nor independent confirmation that Rule Miner's output measurably shapes future review behavior. missing for 10: hands-on/independent evidence that Rule Miner-derived rules actually change future PR reviews, evidence of learning from dismissed/discussed findings, and detail on how conflicting or evolving conventions are reconciled over time.
